notes: Difficulty 3. Acceptance is independent of the run's own reading twice over: the CHECKS measure the assembly (envelope, exact volume including the 8 mm bore, flush contact with the seeded wall gauge) and the grader generates the dimensioned sheet itself and extracts its PDF text layer, requiring the five principal dimensions (600.0 / 250.0 / 218.0 overall, 18.0 material thickness, dia 8.0 bore) - which are the drawing's engineering purpose and are the model's own dimensions, so a run that draws a wrong shelf fails the drawing requirement and not just the checks. Re-authored 2026-07-26 (corpus audit): the title block's material line was gated as a VERBATIM string ('18 mm Baltic birch plywood'), which is a reproduction demand - correct runs failed on punctuation. The metadata is now gated structurally instead (metadata_requirements): the six §5.2 fields must be authored, the process must be the 'laser_cut' pack id, and the free-text material_spec must RESOLVE in the materials registry to plywood-baltic-birch, so any wording that names the right stock passes. The reference solution is a file overlay, so its call path is counted by hand: 11 calls (read_part rail, read_globals, write_part, build_part, measure, generate_drawing, run_checks plus slack); budget 18 leaves ~60% headroom for the metadata iteration, and dropping the string match did not change the call path. The geometry half was re-authored in the same pass: shelf_material became shelf_material_budget and its window went from +/-50 mm^3 on 4.5 million (one part in 90,000 - an unrequested 0.5 mm break on one 600 mm edge is 75) to +/-350, which is still 2.6x below the missing cable bore (905 mm^3) it has to reject.
